texts.preamble: Sunil Baisoya vs State Through Food Safety Officer on 4 August, 2025 In The Court Of Sh. Virender Kumar Bansal Principal District & Sessions Judge/ Food Safety Appellate Tribunal/ New Delhi District, Patiala House Courts, New Delhi Fsat No. 14/2023 Cnr No. Dlnd01-005958-2023 1. Sunil Baisoya S/o. Sh. Attar Singh R/o. P-133, Pilangi Village, Sarojini Nagar, New Delhi-110023 ....... Appe Versus State through Food Safety Officer Department of Food Safety, Govt. of Nct of Delhi, 8th Floor, Mayur Bhawan, Shanker Market, Connaught Place, New Delhi-110001 ....... Resp Date of institution : 07.07.2023 Arguments heard on : 02.08.2025 Date of Judgment : 04.08.2025 Appearances: Sh. M.L. Narang, Ld. Counsel for the appellant. Sh. Birender Singh Dagar, Ld. Chief Public Prosecutor for the State/ Food Safety Officer. Judgment
texts.facts: 1. The present appeal has been preferred impugning the order dated 24.05.2023 whereby the Ld. ADM (South-East) reached to the conclusion that the appellant herein, who was respondent No.2 before the Ld. ADM, was guilty U/s. 26(1) & 26(2)(ii) read with Section 3(1)(zx) of The Food Safety VIRENDER Digitally signed by VIRENDER KUMAR KUMAR BANSAL Date: 2025.08.04 BANSAL 16:37:19 +0530 and Standards Act, 2006 (in short FSS Act) and imposed a penalty of Rs.1,20,000/-. 2. The facts in brief giving rise to the present appeal are that on 25.05.2019 Ms. Anjali Bhardwaj, the Food Safety Officer, lifted the sample of "Buffalo Milk" from Ajay Kumar, the servant of the appellant herein. The sample so lifted was put in four bottles and was sealed in accordance with the rules. The sample was analyzed and was found deficient in milk solid not fat. Accordingly, an application was filed before the Ld. ADM who passed an order dated 24.05.2023, which is impugned in the present appeal. Sunil Baisoya vs State Through Food Safety Officer on 4 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158401646/ 1 3. Notice of the appeal was given to the State/FSO. Record of the Ld. ADM was also summoned. Ld. Counsel submitted that in this case, according to the story of the prosecution, the samples were taken on 25.05.2019. The report of the analyst has been received on 10.06.2019 and notice was given to Sh. Ajay Kumar on 01.06.2019 giving him an opportunity to file appeal against the impugned order.
texts.arguments: 5. Ld. Counsel submitted that the order passed by the Ld. ADM is not in accordance with rules and law and also not based upon the facts of the case resulting into miscarriage of justice. Ld. Counsel submitted that as per Section 77 of the FSS Act, the limitation for Court to take cognizance is one year and no Court shall take cognizance after expiry of the period of one year from the date of commission of the offence. Ld. Counsel submitted that delay has not been explained and the Court shall not condone the delay without any sufficient cause being shown. Here in the present case, the prosecution has been initiated after one year and hence barred by limitation. Ld. Counsel in support of his arguments relied upon the judgment cited as State of Uttar Pradesh through Executive Engineer and Another Vs. Amar Nath Yadav, [(2014) 2 SCC 422]. 6. Ld. Chief Public Prosecutor for the FSO submitted that in this case the prosecution has been initiated within one year and there is no delay except due to the reason that Ms. Anjali Bhardwaj, Food Safety Officer, who took the sample proceeded on maternity leave. Para 10 of the application itself mentions the extension of time, which reads as under : "That the Worthy Commissioner (Food Safety) granted extension time of 08 months beyond one year time limit under Section 77 of the Food Safety and Standards At, 2006 on request of the undersigned, which was forwarded by the Designated Officer concerned for completing pending investigation and launching prosecution." 7. Ld. Chief Public Prosecutor for the FSO has submitted that though the limitation is one year but the proviso to the Section empowers the Commissioner of Food Safety to extend the time and that has been done by the Commissioner of Food Safety and hence the prosecution, which has been launched on 16.07.2020 is within limitation. It is submitted that there is no merit in the contentions raised and on that ground no benefit can be given to the appellant herein. VIRENDER by KUMAR KUM The Section also provides that the Commissioner of Food Safety may, for the reasons to be recorded in writing, approve prosecution within an extended period of upto three years. 9. Ld. Counsel further submitted that the appellant has not received the copy of the report of food analyst along with notice U/s.46(4) of the Act, which is mandatory in nature and he has been deprived of his valuable right. Chief Public Prosecutor for the FSO submitted that the Food Safety & Standards Rules, 2011, Rule 2.4.1.4 provides as under : VIRENDER by VIRENDER KUMAR KUMAR BANSAL Date: 2025.08.04 BANSAL 16:37:46 +0530 "2.4: Sampling and Analysis 2.4.1: Procedure for taking sample and manner of sending it for analysis - The Food Safety Officer while taking sample of food for analysis under clause A of Sub Section 1 of Section 38 and Section 47 (except 47 (5)) of the Act, shall also follow the procedure specified hereunder;- 4. in case the food business operator discloses that the product has been obtained from the manufacturer, the distributor or supplier, a notice shall also be given to such manufacturer, distributor or supplier." 11. In case the Food business operator from whom the sample has been taken or the person whose name and address and other particulars have been disclosed under Rule 2.5 of these rules, desires to have the fourth part of the sample analysed, he shall request the Food Safety Officer in writing to send the sample to any NABL accredited/ FSSAI notified laboratory for analysis under intimation to the Designated Sunil Baisoya vs State Through Food Safety Officer on 4 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158401646/ 3 Officer. 2. Provided that the cost of testing by the accredited lab will be borne by the Food Business Operator or the person identified under Rule 2.5. Ld. Counsel submitted that such marginal variation can be due to wrong sampling or even due to analytical error and hence benefit be given to him. Ld. Counsel in support of his arguments relied upon the judgment cited as Delhi Administration Vs. Balak Ram [(2024) (2) FAC 49] wherein the difference in milk solid not fat were analyzed and there was variation of .2% and given the benefit. 16. Ld. Chief Public Prosecutor for the FSO submitted that firstly it is not marginal variation.
